title_en: Amendment (VIII) to the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: 1. One article is added after Article 17 of the Criminal Law, as Article 17a: "A person who has attained the age of 75 and intentionally commits a crime may be given a lighter or mitigated punishment; a person who commits a crime negligently shall be given a lighter or mitigated punishment."

2. One paragraph is added to Article 38 of the Criminal Law as paragraph 2: "Where public surveillance is imposed, the criminal may be prohibited, in light of the circumstances of the crime, from engaging in specified activities, entering specified areas or venues, or contacting specified persons during the period of enforcement."
The original paragraph 2 is changed to paragraph 3 and amended to read: "A criminal who is sentenced to public surveillance shall be subjected to community correction according to law."
One paragraph is added as paragraph 4: "A person who violates the restraining order provided in paragraph 2 shall be punished by the public security organ in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Penalties for Administration of Public Security."

3. One paragraph is added to Article 49 of the Criminal Law as paragraph 2: "The death penalty shall not be applied to a person who has attained the age of 75 at the time of adjudication, except where death is caused by especially cruel means."

4. Article 50 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "Where a person is sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, if no intentional crime is committed during the period of the reprieve, the sentence shall be commuted to life imprisonment upon expiration of the two-year period; if major meritorious service is actually performed, the sentence shall be commuted to fixed-term imprisonment of 25 years upon expiration of the two-year period; if an intentional crime is committed and it is verified, the death penalty shall be executed upon approval by the Supreme People's Court.
"For a recidivist sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve or a criminal sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve for intentional homicide, rape, robbery, kidnapping, arson, explosion, dissemination of dangerous substances, or organized violent crimes, the People's Court may, in light of the circumstances of the crime, concurrently decide to restrict commutation of punishment."

5. Paragraph 1 of Article 63 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "Where a criminal has a circumstance for mitigated punishment prescribed in this Law, the sentence shall be imposed below the statutory punishment; where this Law provides for several sentencing ranges, the sentence shall be imposed within the next sentencing range below the statutory sentencing range."

6. Paragraph 1 of Article 65 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A criminal who is sentenced to a punishment of fixed-term imprisonment or above, and within five years after completion of the enforcement or after pardon, commits another crime that shall be sentenced to a punishment of fixed-term imprisonment or above, is a recidivist and shall be given a severe punishment; however, this shall not apply to negligent crimes or crimes committed by a person under the age of 18."

7. Article 66 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A criminal who commits a crime endangering national security, a terrorist activity crime, or an organized crime of a mafia-like nature who, after completion of the enforcement or after pardon, again commits any of the aforesaid categories of crimes at any time shall be treated as a recidivist."

8. One paragraph is added to Article 67 of the Criminal Law as paragraph 3: "A criminal suspect who, although not having the circumstances of voluntary surrender as provided in the preceding two paragraphs, truthfully confesses his own crime may be given a lighter punishment; if, because of such truthful confession, especially serious consequences are avoided, a mitigated punishment may be given."
9. Paragraph 2 of Article 68 of the Criminal Law is deleted.

10. Article 69 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "Where a person commits several crimes before a judgment is pronounced, unless he is sentenced to death or life imprisonment, the term of sentence to be executed shall be determined by discretion within the total term of the punishments and above the maximum term of the punishments imposed for the individual crimes, provided that the maximum term of public surveillance shall not exceed three years, the maximum term of criminal detention shall not exceed one year, and the maximum term of fixed-term imprisonment shall not exceed 20 years if the total term is less than 35 years, or shall not exceed 25 years if the total term is 35 years or more.
"Where supplementary punishments are imposed for several crimes, the supplementary punishments shall still be executed; if the supplementary punishments are of the same type, they shall be executed concurrently; if they are of different types, they shall be executed separately."

11. Article 72 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "For a criminal who is sentenced to criminal detention or fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, probation may be declared if the following conditions are concurrently met; for a person under the age of 18, a pregnant woman, or a person who has attained the age of 75, probation shall be declared:
"(1) the circumstances of the crime are minor;
"(2) there is evidence of repentance;
"(3) there is no danger of committing further crimes; and
"(4) the declaration of probation will not have a significant adverse impact on the community in which the sentenced person resides.
"Where probation is declared, the criminal may be prohibited, in light of the circumstances of the crime, from engaging in specified activities, entering specified areas or venues, or contacting specified persons during the probation period.
"If a criminal declared with probation is sentenced to supplementary punishments, the supplementary punishments shall still be executed."
12. Article 74 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "Probation shall not be applied to recidivists or ringleaders of criminal groups."

13. Article 76 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "For a criminal who is declared with probation, community correction shall be implemented according to law during the probation period. If there is no circumstance provided in Article 77 of this Law, upon expiration of the probation period, the original sentence shall no longer be executed, and shall be publicly announced."

14. Paragraph 2 of Article 77 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "Where a criminal who is declared with probation, during the probation period, violates the laws, administrative regulations, or the supervisory provisions on probation of the relevant departments under the State Council, or violates a restraining order in the judgment of the People's Court, if the circumstances are serious, the probation shall be revoked and the original sentence shall be executed."

15. Paragraph 2 of Article 78 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "The term of sentence actually executed after commutation of punishment shall not be less than the following periods:
"(1) for a person sentenced to public surveillance, criminal detention, or fixed-term imprisonment, not less than one-half of the original term of sentence;
"(2) for a person sentenced to life imprisonment, not less than 13 years; and
"(3) for a criminal sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve whose commutation of punishment is restricted by the People's Court in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 50 of this Law, if the sentence is commuted to life imprisonment after expiration of the reprieve period according to law, not less than 25 years; if the sentence is commuted to fixed-term imprisonment of 25 years after expiration of the reprieve period according to law, not less than 20 years."

16. Article 81 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A criminal sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment who has served more than one-half of the original term of sentence, or a criminal sentenced to life imprisonment who has actually served at least 13 years, may be granted parole if he earnestly observes prison regulations, accepts education and reform, shows true repentance, and has no danger of committing further crimes. Where there are special circumstances, the restriction on the above term of enforcement may be lifted upon approval by the Supreme People's Court.
"Parole shall not be granted to recidivists or to criminals who are sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of 10 years or more or life imprisonment for intentional homicide, rape, robbery, kidnapping, arson, explosion, dissemination of dangerous substances, or organized violent crimes.
"When deciding on parole for a criminal, the impact of the parole on the community in which the parolee resides shall be taken into consideration."

17. Article 85 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "For a criminal who is granted parole, community correction shall be implemented according to law during the parole period. If there is no circumstance provided in Article 86 of this Law, upon expiration of the parole period, the original sentence shall be deemed to have been fully executed, and shall be publicly announced."

18. Paragraph 3 of Article 86 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "Where a criminal who is granted parole, during the parole period, commits acts that violate the laws, administrative regulations, or the supervisory provisions on parole of the relevant departments under the State Council, but which do not constitute a new crime, parole shall be revoked according to legal procedures, and the criminal shall be taken back into custody to serve the remainder of the sentence."

19. One paragraph is added to Article 100 of the Criminal Law as paragraph 2: "A person who was under the age of 18 when the crime was committed and was sentenced to a punishment of fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years shall be exempted from the reporting obligation provided in the preceding paragraph."

20. Article 107 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "Where any domestic or foreign institution, organization or individual provides financial support for the commission of a crime provided for in Articles 102, 103, 104, or 105 of this Chapter, the person directly responsible shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention, public surveillance, or deprivation of political rights; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years."

21. Article 109 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A State functionary who, during the performance of his official duties, deserts his post and flees abroad or deserts abroad shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention, public surveillance, or deprivation of political rights; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than 10 years.
"A State functionary who is in possession of State secrets and flees abroad or deserts abroad shall be given a severe punishment in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph."

22. One article is added after Article 133 of the Criminal Law as Article 133a: "A person who drives a motor vehicle on the road chasing and racing, if the circumstances are egregious, or who drives a motor vehicle on the road while intoxicated, shall be sentenced to criminal detention and a fine.
"Where the act in the preceding paragraph also constitutes another crime, the person shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions for the heavier punishment."

23. Paragraph 1 of Article 141 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who produces or sells counterfeit drugs shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention and a fine; if serious harm is caused to human health or there are other serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than 10 years and a fine; if death is caused or there are other especially serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years, life imprisonment, or death, and a fine or confiscation of property."

24. Article 143 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who produces or sells food that does not meet food safety standards, which is sufficient to cause a serious food poisoning accident or other serious foodborne disease, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention and a fine; if serious harm is caused to human health or there are other serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and a fine; if the consequences are especially serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than seven years or life imprisonment, and a fine or confiscation of property."

25. Article 144 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who mixes food produced or sold with toxic or harmful non-food raw materials, or sells food known to be mixed with such raw materials, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years and a fine; if serious harm is caused to human health or there are other serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than 10 years and a fine; if death is caused or there are other especially serious circumstances, he shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 141 of this Law."

26. Article 151 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who smuggles weapons, ammunition, nuclear materials, or counterfeit currency shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than seven years and a fine or confiscation of property; if the circumstances are especially serious, he shall be sentenced to life imprisonment or death and confiscation of property; if the circumstances are relatively minor, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and a fine.
"A person who smuggles cultural relics, gold, silver, or other precious metals that are prohibited by the State from export, or precious animals and their products that are prohibited by the State from import or export, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than 10 years and a fine; if the circumstances are especially serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years or life imprisonment and confiscation of property; if the circumstances are relatively minor, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years and a fine.
"A person who smuggles rare plants and their products, or other goods and articles that are prohibited by the State from import or export, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention, and/or a fine; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years and a fine.
"Where a unit commits a crime provided for in this Article, a fine shall be imposed on the unit, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the paragraphs of this Article."

27. Paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who smuggles goods or articles other than those provided for in Articles 151, 152, and 347 of this Law shall, in light of the seriousness of the circumstances, be punished respectively in accordance with the following provisions:
"(1) where the amount of tax evaded on the smuggled goods or articles is relatively large, or where a person has been given administrative penalties twice for smuggling within one year and smuggles again, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention, and a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the amount of tax evaded;
"(2) where the amount of tax evaded on the smuggled goods or articles is huge, or there are other serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than 10 years, and a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the amount of tax evaded; and
"(3) where the amount of tax evaded on the smuggled goods or articles is especially huge, or there are other especially serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years or life imprisonment, and a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the amount of tax evaded or confiscation of property."

28. Paragraph 1 of Article 157 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who smuggles with armed escort shall be given a severe punishment in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1 of Article 151 of this Law."

29. Article 164 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who gives property to a staff member of a company, enterprise, or other unit for the purpose of seeking illegitimate benefits, if the amount is relatively large, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention; if the amount is huge, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than 10 years and a fine.
"A person who gives property to a foreign public official or an official of an international public organization for the purpose of seeking illegitimate commercial benefits shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
"Where a unit commits the crime in the preceding two paragraphs, a fine shall be imposed on the unit, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1.
"A bribe-giver who voluntarily confesses the bribe-giving before being prosecuted may be given a mitigated punishment or be exempted from punishment."

30. Article 199 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who commits a crime provided for in Article 192 of this Section, if the amount is especially huge and causes especially heavy losses to the interests of the State and the people, shall be sentenced to life imprisonment or death and confiscation of property."

31. Article 200 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "Where a unit commits a crime provided for in Article 192, 194, or 195 of this Section, a fine shall be imposed on the unit, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention, and may also be fined; if the amount is huge or there are other serious circumstances, they shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than 10 years and a fine; if the amount is especially huge or there are other especially serious circumstances, they shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years or life imprisonment and a fine."
32. Paragraph 2 of Article 205 of the Criminal Law is deleted.

33. One article is added after Article 205 of the Criminal Law as Article 205a: "A person who falsely issues invoices other than those provided for in Article 205 of this Law, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than two years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and a fine; if the circumstances are especially serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than two years but not more than seven years and a fine.
"Where a unit commits the crime in the preceding paragraph, a fine shall be imposed on the unit, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph."
34. Paragraph 2 of Article 206 of the Criminal Law is deleted.

35. One article is added after Article 210 of the Criminal Law as Article 210a: "A person who knowingly holds counterfeit invoices, if the quantity is relatively large, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than two years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and a fine; if the quantity is huge, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than two years but not more than seven years and a fine.
"Where a unit commits the crime in the preceding paragraph, a fine shall be imposed on the unit, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph."

37. One article is added after Article 234 of the Criminal Law as Article 234a: "A person who organizes others to sell human organs shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years and a fine; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years and a fine or confiscation of property.
"A person who removes an organ without the consent of the person concerned, or removes an organ of a person under the age of 18, or forces or deceives another person to donate an organ, shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions of Articles 234 and 232 of this Law.
"A person who, contrary to the will of a person during his lifetime, removes an organ from his corpse, or, without express consent during his lifetime, in violation of State regulations, contrary to the will of his close relative, removes an organ from his corpse, shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 302 of this Law."

38. Article 244 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who forces another person to work by means of violence, threat, or restriction of personal freedom shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention and a fine; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than 10 years and a fine.
"A person who, knowing that another person is committing the act in the preceding paragraph, recruits or transports persons for him, or otherwise assists in forcing another person to work, shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
"Where a unit commits the crime in the preceding two paragraphs, a fine shall be imposed on the unit, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 1."

39. Article 264 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who steals public or private property, if the amount is relatively large, or who commits multiple thefts, burglary, theft with a weapon, or pickpocketing, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and/or a fine; if the amount is huge or there are other serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than 10 years and a fine; if the amount is especially huge or there are other especially serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years or life imprisonment, and a fine or confiscation of property."

40. Article 274 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who extorts public or private property, if the amount is relatively large or if he commits multiple extortions, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and/or a fine; if the amount is huge or there are other serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than 10 years and a fine; if the amount is especially huge or there are other especially serious circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years and a fine."

41. One article is added after Article 276 of the Criminal Law as Article 276a: "A person who, by means of transferring property, absconding, or other methods, evades paying laborers' labor remuneration, or who has the ability to pay but does not pay laborers' labor remuneration, if the amount is relatively large, and after being ordered by the relevant government department to pay, still fails to pay, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention, and/or a fine; if serious consequences are caused, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and a fine.
"Where a unit commits the crime in the preceding paragraph, a fine shall be imposed on the unit, and the directly responsible supervisor and other directly liable persons shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.
"A person who commits the act in the preceding two paragraphs, but does not cause serious consequences, and pays laborers' labor remuneration before a public prosecution is initiated and bears corresponding compensation liability according to law, may be given a mitigated punishment or be exempted from punishment."

43. Article 294 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who organizes or leads a mafia-like organization shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than seven years and confiscation of property; a person who actively participates in such an organization shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years, and may also be fined or subjected to confiscation of property; a person who otherwise participates in such an organization shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, public surveillance, or deprivation of political rights, and may also be fined.
"A member of a foreign mafia organization who enters the territory of the People's Republic of China to develop members shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than 10 years.
"A State functionary who harbors a mafia-like organization or connives at the illegal or criminal activities of a mafia-like organization shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years.
"A person who commits the crimes in the preceding three paragraphs and also commits other crimes shall be punished in accordance with the provisions on combined punishment for multiple crimes.
"A mafia-like organization shall concurrently possess the following characteristics:
"(1) it is a relatively stable criminal organization with a relatively large number of members, with clear organizers and leaders, and core members are basically fixed;
"(2) it systematically obtains economic benefits through illegal or criminal activities or other means, and possesses a certain economic strength to support the activities of the organization;
"(3) it systematically commits multiple illegal or criminal activities by means of violence, threats, or other means, committing evils, oppressing, and harming the masses; and
"(4) through the commission of illegal or criminal activities, or by taking advantage of the harboring or connivance of State functionaries, it dominates a locality, forms illegal control or significant influence in a certain region or industry, thereby seriously disrupting economic and social order."

44. Article 295 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who teaches criminal methods shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention, or public surveillance; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than 10 years; if the circumstances are especially serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years or life imprisonment."

46. Article 338 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who, in violation of State regulations, discharges, dumps, or disposes of radioactive waste, waste containing infectious disease pathogens, toxic substances, or other hazardous substances, thereby causing serious environmental pollution, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention, and/or a fine; if the consequences are especially serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and a fine."

47. Paragraph 1 of Article 343 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who, in violation of the provisions of the Mineral Resources Law, mines without obtaining a mining license, enters a State-planned mining area, a mining area of significant value to the national economy, or another person's mining area to mine, or mines a specific mineral species that the State has designated for protective mining, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and/or a fine; if the circumstances are especially serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than seven years and a fine."

48. Paragraph 3 of Article 358 of the Criminal Law is amended to read: "A person who recruits or transports persons for an organizer of prostitution, or otherwise assists in organizing others to engage in prostitution, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years and a fine; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than 10 years and a fine."

49. One article is added after Article 408 of the Criminal Law as Article 408a: "A State functionary who is responsible for food safety supervision and administration who abuses his power or neglects his duties, thereby causing a major food safety accident or other serious consequences, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention; if especially serious consequences are caused, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than 10 years.
"A person who commits the crime in the preceding paragraph engaging in malpractices for personal gain shall be given a severe punishment."
50. This Amendment shall come into force on May 1, 2011.
